history.new: The exponent-arithmetic fast-forward (Theorem 3) is exact; at L = 1024 it is about two orders of magnitude faster than direct simulation at t = 10^5 (62-100x; the Skeptic's re-run 79-97x) but no faster around t = 10^3 (0.5-1.0x) for L >= 1024, and equal for t < 2L (where it falls back to simulation).
history.old: The exponent-arithmetic fast-forward (Theorem 3) is exact; at L = 1024 it is 62-100x faster than direct simulation at t = 10^5 but 0.5-0.9x (slower) around t = 10^3 for L >= 1024, and equal for t < 2L (where it falls back to simulation).

improvement_detail: wins only for t much larger than L; the O(L^2) product step dominates for moderate t
statement: The exponent-arithmetic fast-forward (Theorem 3) is exact; at L = 1024 it is about two orders of magnitude faster than direct simulation at t = 10^5 (62-100x; the Skeptic's re-run 79-97x) but no faster around t = 10^3 (0.5-1.0x) for L >= 1024, and equal for t < 2L (where it falls back to simulation).
title: Commutative-semigroup fast-forward by exponent arithmetic
